title: Nhat Nguyet: open source code and data for Zi Wei Dou Shu, BaZi and numerology
description:
TypeScript (npm @nhatnguyet/*) and Python (nhatnguyet) libraries, a command line tool, an MCP server and 5 web components for the Vietnamese lunar calendar (Hanoi time, UTC+7) and the Chinese, Korean and Japanese ones, the 24 solar terms, auspicious hours, Zi Wei Dou Shu (Tử Vi), BaZi (Four Pillars), Pythagorean numerology and 206 Vietnamese festivals with provinces, ethnic groups, sourced venues and iCalendar export. English API with results in English, Vietnamese and Chinese; named school options where the classical books disagree, each with its source. No runtime dependencies.

Every result reproduces the reference engine behind nhatnguyet.org (engine 2.2.0) and is checked by 17,291 core test vectors (18,819 including school options and auspicious hours: 14,936 calendar cases, 777 Zi Wei charts, 777 BaZi charts, 600 numerology profiles and 201 festival years, plus 352 Zi Wei and 80 BaZi cases with school options and 1,096 auspicious-hour days) that any port in any language can pass. The calendar is checked against NASA new moons and IMCCE solar terms from 1900 to 2100; on 2,724 of those 73,414 days the Vietnamese lunar date differs from lunar-javascript, which computes the Chinese calendar on Beijing time.

Also in the repository: a terminology dataset (Vietnamese, Chinese, pinyin and English names of every term the libraries output), an AI evaluation set of engine-computed questions, a table of Tết dates 1900 to 2100 as used in Vietnam, a technical report on the calendar method and its verification, and project templates (Next.js, Telegram bot, Google Sheets, Jupyter).

Code: MIT. Data, readings and test vectors: CC BY 4.0. Credit: Data: Nhat Nguyet (nhatnguyet.org).

https://nhatnguyet.org/en/ma-nguon-mo
